title: Amon Darthir
blurb: Amon Darthir was a peak of the Mountains of Shadow, rising above the house of Húrin in Dor-lómin.
book:
Amon Darthir was one of the mountains of Ered Wethrin, the range that walled Dor-lómin on the south. It stood above the home of Húrin and Morwen.

A stream rose from a spring beneath the mountain and ran down past the house. This was Nen Lalaith. The family of Húrin lived in its shadow until the Nirnaeth Arnoediad.

After that war the Easterlings overran Dor-lómin. Morwen stayed on in the house, and she sent her son Túrin away to Doriath.

facts.Location: Ered Wethrin, south of the house of Húrin

sources: The Silmarillion, Of Túrin Turambar
Unfinished Tales, Narn i Hîn Húrin

title: Nen Lalaith
blurb: Nen Lalaith was a stream in Dor-lómin that ran past the house of Húrin and Morwen.
book:
Nen Lalaith was a small stream in Dor-lómin. It rose from a spring on the slopes of Amon Darthir and passed close to the house of Húrin.

The name means Laughing Water. Túrin grew up beside it. His little sister Urwen was also called Lalaith, which means Laughter, but she died young of a plague.

The stream belongs to the happy early years of the family. Those years ended with the Nirnaeth Arnoediad and the Easterling conquest of Dor-lómin.

facts.Location: Below Amon Darthir, beside the house of Húrin

sources: The Silmarillion, Of Túrin Turambar
Unfinished Tales, Narn i Hîn Húrin

title: Annon-in-Gelydh
kind: Hidden gate of the Noldor in Dor-lómin
blurb: Annon-in-Gelydh was a secret gate of the Noldor in the western hills of Dor-lómin, which Tuor found with the help of Ulmo.
book:
Annon-in-Gelydh was the Gate of the Noldor. It lay in the western hills of Dor-lómin, where a stream ran into the rock. The Noldor had made it long before, and it was kept secret from the servants of Morgoth.

Ulmo guided Tuor son of Huor to the gate. Tuor followed the stream through the dark tunnel and came out in Cirith Ninniach, the Rainbow Cleft, near the sea.

From there Tuor went on to Nevrast. He later reached Gondolin by the secret road.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin
Unfinished Tales, Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin

title: Caves of Androth
kind: Caves in the hills of Mithrim
blurb: The Caves of Androth were hill caves in Mithrim where Tuor lived among the Grey-elves after the Nirnaeth Arnoediad.
book:
Androth lay in the hills of Mithrim. After the Nirnaeth Arnoediad a few Grey-elves lived there in caves. Tuor, the son of Huor, was fostered among them as a child.

His foster-father there was the elf Annael. Tuor grew up in the care of this small band.

When Tuor was sixteen, the Easterlings captured him, and he served as a thrall for three years. He escaped and lived as an outlaw in the hills. Then Ulmo sent him to the hidden gate of the Noldor.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin
Unfinished Tales, Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin

title: Dry River
kind: Dry bed of the hidden way to Gondolin
blurb: The Dry River was an empty stream-bed near the Brithiach that led Voronwë and Tuor toward the hidden gate of Gondolin.
book:
The Dry River was the bed of an old stream that no longer carried water. Long ago it had flowed out of the vale of Tumladen toward the river Sirion, close to the ford of Brithiach.

Its channel gave a hidden path into the land of Gondolin. The people of Turgon kept the way secret.

The Elf Voronwë led Tuor along it to the hidden gate. Beyond lay Orfalch Echor, the great ravine of the seven gates that led into Tumladen.

facts.Location: Near the Brithiach, on the way to Orfalch Echor

sources: The Silmarillion, Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin
Unfinished Tales, Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin

title: Cairn of Fingolfin
kind: Cairn of the High King of the Noldor
blurb: Turgon raised a cairn on a mountain north of Gondolin over the body of his father Fingolfin.
book:
Fingolfin, High King of the Noldor, fought Morgoth in single combat before the gates of Angband. He wounded the Dark Lord seven times, but he was slain.

Thorondor, King of the Eagles, rescued his body. He bore it north of Gondolin to a high peak of the mountains that surround the hidden city.

Turgon, the son of Fingolfin, laid his father there and raised a cairn. The servants of Morgoth never dared to disturb it.

facts.Location: Peak on the north of the Encircling Mountains

sources: The Silmarillion, Of the Ruin of Beleriand and the Fall of Fingolfin

title: Cairn of Glorfindel
kind: Cairn of the lord of the Golden Flower
blurb: A cairn stood beside Cirith Thoronath over Glorfindel, who died fighting a Balrog during the escape from Gondolin.
book:
Glorfindel was a lord of Gondolin. In the fall of the city he helped the refugees of Tuor and Idril to escape over the mountains.

At Cirith Thoronath, the Cleft of the Eagles, a Balrog attacked the company. Glorfindel fought it on a narrow ledge. Both fell from the height.

Thorondor brought up his body from the abyss. The refugees buried him in a mound of stones beside the pass, and green turf later grew on it. They then passed on toward the Sirion.

facts.Location: Beside Cirith Thoronath, in the northern mountains

sources: The Silmarillion, Of the Fall of Gondolin

title: Stone of the Hapless
blurb: The Stone of the Hapless stood on the mound of Túrin above Cabed-en-Aras. It also bore the name of his sister Nienor.
book:
Túrin Turambar killed the dragon Glaurung at Cabed-en-Aras, a gorge of the river Teiglin. Soon after, Nienor learned that her husband was her own brother. She leapt into the gorge, and the river took her.

Túrin then took his own life on his sword Gurthang. He was laid in a high mound, and a great grey stone was set upon it.

The stone bore the names of Túrin and of Nienor, but her body was never found. Later Húrin came to the place and found Morwen there. She died beside the stone.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Túrin Turambar
Unfinished Tales, Narn i Hîn Húrin

title: Celebros
blurb: The Celebros was a stream in Brethil that fell over Nen Girith and flowed into the Teiglin.
book:
The Celebros rose in the forest of Brethil and ran down its high ground. It fell in a waterfall called Nen Girith and joined the river Teiglin.

The forest of Brethil was home to the Haladin, the people of Haleth.

When Níniel first came to Nen Girith, a sudden shuddering came upon her. Later Túrin and the men of Brethil watched for Glaurung from the falls before they went down to Cabed-en-Aras.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Túrin Turambar

title: Haudh-en-Arwen
blurb: Haudh-en-Arwen, the Ladybarrow, was the green mound of Haleth, chieftain of the Haladin, in the heights of Brethil.
book:
Haleth was a woman who led the Haladin, a people of Men. She defended them against the orcs and later brought them to the forest of Brethil.

When she died, her people buried her in a green mound in the heights of the forest. It was called Haudh-en-Arwen, the Ladybarrow.

The Haladin dwelt in Brethil for many years after her death.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of the Coming of Men into the West
Unfinished Tales

title: Hírilorn
blurb: Hírilorn was the greatest beech of Neldoreth, where Thingol shut Lúthien in a house high in its branches.
book:
Hírilorn was a huge beech in the forest of Neldoreth. It had three trunks and stood in Doriath.

Thingol wished to keep Lúthien from Beren and from danger. He had a house built high in the tree, and he set her there.

Lúthien escaped. She made a cloak from her own hair, and it lulled her guards to sleep. She came down from the tree and went to find Beren.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien

title: Girdle of Melian
blurb: The Girdle of Melian was an unseen wall of enchantment that kept enemies out of Doriath.
book:
Melian was a Maia and the queen of Doriath. She wove a magic round Neldoreth and Region. This was the Girdle of Melian.

No creature could pass it against the will of Melian or Thingol. It kept Morgoth and his servants away from Doriath for many years.

The Girdle failed after Thingol was killed and Melian left Middle-earth. The Dwarves then sacked Menegroth.

facts.Location: Border of Doriath; northern edge shown

sources: The Silmarillion, Of Thingol and Melian
The Silmarillion, Of the Ruin of Doriath

title: Little Gelion
blurb: Little Gelion was the western arm of the river Gelion, rising in the hills of Himring.
book:
The great river Gelion in East Beleriand had two sources. Little Gelion was the western one.

It came down from the hills near the fortress of Himring. Himring was held by Maedhros, son of Fëanor.

The two arms of Gelion met and flowed south as one river. Gelion then reached the land of Ossiriand.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Beleriand and its Realms

title: Greater Gelion
blurb: Greater Gelion was the eastern arm of the river Gelion, rising on Mount Rerir.
book:
Greater Gelion was the larger and more eastern source of the river Gelion. It rose on the slopes of Mount Rerir.

The river ran west and south. It joined Little Gelion, the western arm, and became the single stream of Gelion.

Mount Rerir stood above Lake Helevorn in Thargelion. Caranthir, son of Fëanor, dwelt in that land.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Beleriand and its Realms

title: Dor Firn-i-Guinar
kind: Land where Beren and Lúthien lived again
blurb: Dor Firn-i-Guinar was the name of the land in Ossiriand around Tol Galen where Beren and Lúthien lived after their return.
book:
Beren died after taking the Silmaril from Morgoth. Lúthien followed him to Mandos and moved the Vala Mandos with her song. Both were allowed to return to life, and Lúthien became mortal.

They made their home in Ossiriand near Tol Galen, the Green Isle. The land was called Dor Firn-i-Guinar, the Land of the Dead that Live. Their son Dior was born there.

Beren later took the Nauglamír with the Silmaril from the Dwarves at Sarn Athrad. Lúthien wore it in this land, and after their deaths it passed to Dior.

names.English: Land of the Dead that Live

facts.Meaning: Land of the Dead that Live

sources: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien

title: Dor-Cúarthol
kind: Land held by Túrin and Beleg
blurb: Dor-Cúarthol was the Land of Bow and Helm, held by Túrin and Beleg from their stronghold on Amon Rûdh.
book:
After Túrin left Doriath, he joined a band of outlaws and became their leader. Beleg Cúthalion found him and later came back to join his company.

They made their base on Amon Rûdh. From there they defended the nearby country against orcs. This land took the name Dor-Cúarthol, the Land of Bow and Helm, after the bow of Beleg and the helm of Túrin.

The outlaws lived at the hill with the Petty-dwarf Mîm. Mîm later betrayed their hiding place to the orcs.
sources: The Silmarillion, Of Túrin Turambar
